content.title: What are the weight categories in the UFC?
content.text: UFC Weight Classes: The Fight Structure The UFC (Ultimate Fighting Championship) is the premier Mixed Martial Arts organization and its division system is the global standard. Understanding weight classes is not just about numbers; it’s about grasping the strategy, speed, and power that define each matchup in the octagon. From the fast exchanges in flyweight to the devastating power of heavyweights, each division has its own identity. Official Divisions and Weight Limits Table Below, we detail the exact limits fighters must meet on the official scale (excluding the one-pound tolerance allowed in non-title fights). Division (Name) Limit (Pounds) Limit (Kg) Gender Strawweight (Strawweight) 115 lbs 52.2 kg Female Flyweight (Flyweight) 125 lbs 56.7 kg Male / Female Bantamweight (Bantamweight) 135 lbs 61.2 kg Male / Female Featherweight (Featherweight) 145 lbs 65.8 kg Male / Female Lightweight (Lightweight) 155 lbs 70.3 kg Male Welterweight (Welterweight) 170 lbs 77.1 kg Male Middleweight (Middleweight) 185 lbs 83.9 kg Male Light Heavyweight (Light Heavyweight) 205 lbs 93.0 kg Male Heavyweight (Heavyweight) 265 lbs 120.2 kg Male Official Equipment by Category Regardless of weight, all athletes must use approved equipment to ensure physical integrity. At España, we distribute the official brands you see on TV. 4oz Gloves: Mandatory to allow grappling while maintaining knuckle protection. Compression/Fight Shorts: Designed not to limit mobility on high kicks nor offer grips to the opponent. Protection: Mandatory use of groin guard and mouthguard. Expert Advice: The "Weight Cut" Do not try to imitate professional weight cuts. A lightweight fighter (70kg) may normally walk around at 85kg. Extreme dehydration to make weight is dangerous and should be supervised by medical professionals and sports nutritionists. For your training, prioritize your natural weight and long-term health. What happens if a fighter misses weight? If an athlete exceeds the limit, they are usually fined 20% or 30% of their purse, which goes to their opponent. The fight can take place at a "Catchweight" (agreed weight) if the opponent agrees. Are there more weight classes? Yes, there are divisions like Atomweight (under 105 lbs) or Super Heavyweight (over 265 lbs), but these are currently not part of the active UFC structure. Are the gloves the same for all categories? Generally yes, 4-ounce gloves are used. However, in some commissions and higher categories (XL to 2XL hand size), the glove must be adapted to the fighter’s hand size, although the padding weight remains standard for professional competition.
